name: Salt Lake City & Park City
summary: Utah's capital between the mountains and the great salt lake — Temple Square and the statehouse, and the Olympic ski town of Park City up the canyon.

foodMustTry.blurb: Utah's ketchup-mayo staple, and the local Crown Burger classic.

item.title: Temple Square

location.name: Temple Square
location.address: 50 N Temple, Salt Lake City, UT

item.blurb: The centre of the Latter-day Saint world — ten acres of gardens, the Tabernacle with its famous acoustics, and the temple itself, which non-members don't enter.

item.title: The Utah State Capitol

location.name: Utah State Capitol
location.address: 350 State St, Salt Lake City, UT

item.blurb: It stands on the bench above the city with the whole Salt Lake Valley below it and the Wasatch behind, which is the best free view in Utah. Granite and Georgian marble, a rotunda painted with the state's history, and a seismic retrofit that rests the entire building on 280 base isolators so it can slide two feet in an earthquake.

item.title: Utah Olympic Park & the Alf Engen Ski Museum
item.blurb: The 2002 Winter Games left Park City the best public ski museum in the country and a set of venues that never went quiet. Watch the national team throw itself off the ninety- and one-twenty-metre jumps into a swimming pool, ride a bobsled down the real Olympic track with a professional driver, and walk the Alf Engen Ski Museum, which is free and tells the story of skiing in the Wasatch — the snow here is the reason any of this is in Utah.

item.title: Park City Main Street
item.blurb: A silver-mining boomtown that ran out of silver and found something better under the same mountains. The Victorian main street climbs away from the base of the lifts; Sundance takes the whole town over every January.
